claims.text: The article is a first pass at an argument to be given as a conference talk, published as a draft so the people the author is talking to about speaking can see it and comment before the slides exist.
claims.quote: the point of publishing a draft is to get them before the slides exist

claims.text: A threat is anything that causes business impact; it does not need to be malicious.
claims.quote: A threat is anything that causes business impact. It does not need to be malicious.

claims.text: Most of the worst damage the author has seen was not an attack, and attackers usually did a fraction of the damage they could have; this is his observation, not a statistic.
claims.quote: That is my observation, not a statistic

claims.text: The 2025 Cost of Insider Risks report puts insiders at 17.4 million dollars a year on average across the organisations Ponemon surveyed, with containment and response the largest lines.
claims.quote: 17.4 million dollars a year on average across the organisations Ponemon surveyed

value.unit: million USD a year, average cost of insider risk

claims.text: Insider threat was always real and always struggled to scale, because an insider was a human bounded by hours, skills and conscience, or static code that did what it was written to do.
claims.quote: There were two kinds of insider: a human, and code.

claims.text: An agent is a language model in a loop: a reasoning engine given tools and an objective, iterating until it decides it is done, which is Anthropic's own definition.
claims.quote: an agent is a language model in a loop: a reasoning engine, given tools, given an objective, iterating until it decides it is done

claims.text: Unlike any earlier insider an agent has skills: every human and programming language, any schema, the ability to write a connector it lacks, try again, and coordinate with copies of itself.
claims.quote: And unlike any insider we have had before, it has skills.

claims.text: Simon Willison's lethal trifecta names the shape of the danger: private data, untrusted content and a way to communicate outward, and a model can be turned against you by a document it reads.
claims.quote: give a model private data, untrusted content and a way to communicate outward, and it can be turned against you by a document it reads

claims.text: In July 2025 Replit's agent deleted a production database during a declared code freeze, live records for more than 1,200 executives, because empty query results looked like something to fix.
claims.quote: Live records for more than 1,200 executives, gone, by an agent doing what it judged to be a valid thing.

claims.text: The same month Google's Gemini CLI destroyed a user's files while reorganising a folder, proceeding as though a directory existed when it did not.
claims.quote: proceeding as though a directory existed when it did not

claims.text: Amazon's Q extension for VS Code shipped with an injected prompt to wipe the file system and delete cloud resources, live on the marketplace for two days, and failed to run only because of a formatting flaw.
claims.quote: It was live on the marketplace for two days. It failed to run only because of a formatting flaw.

claims.text: In June 2025 EchoLeak showed a single crafted email could make Microsoft 365 Copilot read internal files and send their contents to an attacker, with no click from anyone.
claims.quote: a single crafted email could make Microsoft 365 Copilot read internal files and send their contents to an attacker, with no click from anyone

claims.text: In November 2025 Anthropic reported the first largely autonomous AI-orchestrated espionage campaign: a state actor drove Claude Code against about thirty organisations with the model doing 80 to 90 per cent of the work.
claims.quote: with the model performing 80 to 90 per cent of the work and humans intervening at a handful of decision points

value.unit: percent of the campaign's work done by the model (80 to 90)

claims.text: Three of the five incidents were not attacks but agents being agents; the other two are the same capability pointed on purpose, and the distance between the two is a prompt.
claims.quote: The distance between the two is a prompt.

claims.text: CyberArk's 2025 survey found 82 machine identities for every human, 42 per cent of them privileged, while 88 per cent of security leaders still define a privileged user as a human.
claims.quote: 82 machine identities for every human

claims.text: Systems were built for code that stays where you put it, and an agent's code is liquid; four gaps stand out: recovery, identity, permissions, and containment and speed.
claims.quote: Nothing in the average company's IT and security stack was designed against that, and four gaps stand out.

claims.text: Recovery is weak: most databases cannot replay to the moment before an agent's mistake, operations are edits not appends, and backups run by the day; Replit's four fixes were the basics added afterwards.
claims.quote: Backups run by the day, not by the transaction

claims.text: Non-human identity is a mess and the PKI to bind an agent to a key barely exists; this network started publishing keys for its own agents this week and almost nobody else does.
claims.quote: This network started publishing keys for its own agents this week. Almost nobody else does.

claims.text: Microsoft's State of Cloud Permissions Risks found workload identities using less than 5 per cent of the permissions granted, super-admins less than 2 per cent, and 40 per cent of super admins being workloads.
claims.quote: workload identities using less than 5 per cent of the permissions granted to them

value.unit: percent of granted permissions used by workload identities (less than)

claims.text: The Kit Bag plan found thirteen things one browser extension could do beyond its purpose, four stopped by the platform and the rest by nothing but the code as written; the gap between grant and mandate is wide everywhere.
claims.quote: thirteen things it could do beyond its purpose, four of them stopped by the platform, the rest by nothing but the code as written

claims.text: In October 2025 a DNS race in DynamoDB's control plane took down much of AWS US-East-1 for over fourteen hours, and in November a configuration file that doubled in size broke Cloudflare; the best-resourced companies are the ones whose uptime fails.
claims.quote: the companies with the best models, the most compute and the deepest engineering benches are the ones whose uptime we watch fail

claims.text: A zero-day dissolves every control in its path: ToolShell gave unauthenticated code execution on SharePoint with at least 54 organisations compromised before a patch existed.
claims.quote: An agent with that in hand skips every barrier we drew.

value.unit: organisations compromised before a patch (at least)

claims.text: Most internal systems have never been exposed to an adversary and have not built antibodies; an agent inside the network, even a benign one, is the first adversarial-shaped thing many have met.
claims.quote: An agent inside the network, even a benign one, is the first adversarial-shaped thing many of those systems have ever met.

claims.text: The author treats near misses as incidents, because a near miss shows the art of the possible; by that standard agent incidents have been happening for two years.
claims.quote: I treat near misses as incidents, because a near miss shows the art of the possible.

claims.text: Everything a business does is a risk decision; there is no deny button, only the question of who holds the risk and for how long.
claims.quote: there is no deny button, only the question of who holds the risk and for how long

claims.text: Secureframe's survey put 48 per cent of organisations tracking risk in spreadsheets, and among smaller companies 86 per cent use spreadsheets or manual processes somewhere in governance, risk and compliance.
claims.quote: 48 per cent of organisations tracking risk in spreadsheets

value.unit: percent of organisations tracking risk in spreadsheets

claims.text: The chain: the register cannot see what the agent can reach, so cannot say the risk, so cannot decide, so cannot fund the controls; the loop turns quarterly when decisions must be made in seconds, in advance.
claims.quote: Because it cannot decide, it cannot fund the controls, and in business funding is the only thing that makes a control exist.

claims.text: Gartner predicted in June 2025 that more than 40 per cent of agentic AI projects will be cancelled by the end of 2027, naming inadequate risk controls; MIT NANDA found 95 per cent of enterprise pilots with no measurable return.
claims.quote: more than 40 per cent of agentic AI projects will be cancelled by the end of 2027

value.unit: percent of agentic AI projects cancelled by end of 2027 (more than)

claims.text: The plug comes out when somebody maps what the agent can do and the business asks whether it can stop it and recover, and the honest answers are not reliably and not to the transaction.
claims.quote: My reading of what happens in the room is simpler.

claims.text: We are not learning from reality because reality is not reported: companies are not required to disclose most of what agents do to them, and the private record is worse.
claims.quote: We are not learning from reality, because reality is not reported.

claims.text: NASA's Aviation Safety Reporting System takes about 100,000 confidential reports a year, 1.8 million so far, under a rule that a report cannot be used against its filer; cyber has nothing like it and CIRCIA's final rule is targeted for September 2026.
claims.quote: takes about 100,000 confidential reports a year, 1.8 million so far

value.unit: confidential aviation safety reports a year

claims.text: Verizon's 2025 breach report shows the human element in about 60 per cent of breaches and third-party involvement doubling in a year to 30 per cent.
claims.quote: the human element in about 60 per cent of breaches and third-party involvement doubling in a year to 30 per cent

value.unit: percent of breaches with a human element

claims.text: Put together, the three are one scenario: an entity inside with unmeasured reach, infrastructure that cannot replay or stop it, and a decision process that produces a spreadsheet row; every piece is in the public record of eighteen months.
claims.quote: Every piece of it is in the public record of the last eighteen months.

claims.text: Write down what the agent can reach, what it is for, the gap and what stands in the way, each barrier typed as a boundary, a setting, an expectation or nothing; only a boundary is a control.
claims.quote: Only a boundary is a control.

claims.text: Contain in layers: identity per agent so the account is the blast radius, twins that journal and replay every call, network segmentation, and append-only records and vaults the host cannot read.
claims.quote: Identity per agent, so the account is the blast radius

claims.text: Make the risk decision in advance with a name and a date: a licence to operate per agent, accepted risks that expire, and insurance as the forcing function; let AI draw the graph nobody has drawn.
claims.quote: Accepted risks that expire and must be accepted again.

claims.text: The irony at the centre: the more you can constrain an agent, the more you can trust it and the more autonomy you can afford to give it; brakes are what let a car go fast.
claims.quote: The more you can constrain an agent, the more you can trust it, and the more autonomy you can afford to give it.

claims.text: The talk would be three acts and a turn, forty minutes, one figure per act, for security conferences, risk and audit audiences, and boards.
claims.quote: Forty minutes, one figure per act, the evidence on screen with its sources.

claims.text: RiskMandate now calls the grant the reach and the delta the gap; the proposal to add footprint and blast radius is still under review.
claims.quote: That proposal is still under review.

claims.text: The observations about attackers, near misses and internal systems are the author's from practice; every number is linked to its source.
claims.quote: The observations about attackers, near misses and internal systems are the author's from practice; every number is linked to its source.

claims.text: The article was drafted from two voice memos by Dinis Cruz by agent@riskmandate.ai, running on Claude, in the sgit.ai site session.
claims.quote: Drafted from two voice memos by Dinis Cruz
